 Order

Accused Nos.1 to 4 are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in Crime No.174/2023 registered by Humnabad Police Station, Bidar for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 324, 504, 506, 448 R/w 149 of IPC.

2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that in respect of the incident that had taken place on 12.08.2023, FIR in Crime No.172/2023 was registered against respondent No.2 herein and others and as a counter to the same, the impugned proceedings has been initiated.
He submits that only to harass and coerce the petitioners, a false complaint has been registered.
He also submits that continuation of impugned proceedings would amount to abuse process of law.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and learned counsel for respondent No.2 have opposed the petition.
They submit that there is a case and counter case in respect of the incident that had taken place on 12.08.2023 and in both the cases, the police after investigation have filed charge sheet.
Accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.

5. The material on record would go to show that in respect of the incident that had taken place on 12.08.2023 in the house of Srikanth who is the husband of petitioner No.1 herein, FIR in Crime No.172/2023 was registered by Humnabad Police Station as against Srikanth and his parents for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 323 & 324 R/w 34 of IPC.
In the said case, the first information was submitted by petitioner No.1 herein on 13.08.2023 at about 17.30 hours.

In respect of the very same incident that had taken place on 12.08.2023, FIR in Crime No.174/2023 was registered by Humnabad Police Station as against the petitioners herein and NC:
2024:KHC-K:3599 another on the first information received from Srikanth on 14.08.2023 at 18.30 hours.
6. Undisputedly, the incident in question has taken place on 12.08.2023.
There cannot be any dispute with regard to the said incident nor there can be any dispute about presence of accused at the spot.
Both the parties have suffered injuries in the incident in question.
It is brought to the notice of this Court that the police after investigation have filed charge sheet in both the cases.

entities.text: Maya And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A case and counter case are criminal cases originating from a single incident that had taken place in any particular area at a specified time or at the same time.

Though the Code of Criminal Procedure or any other statute does not provide as to how the case and counter cases have to be investigated or tried, the courts in order to prevent conflicting decisions with regard to one incident,
have laid down the principles as to how investigation has to be done in a case and counter case NC:
2024:KHC-K:3599 and how the case and counter case are required to be tried.

8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATHI LAL & OTHERS VS STATE OF U.P. - (1990)
Supp. SCC 145, has laid down certain procedures to be followed by the courts in a case and counter case.

entities.text:
NATHI LAL & OTHERS VS STATE OF U.P. - (1990)
Supp. SCC 145
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said judgment was followed in the subsequent judgment in the case of STATE OF M.P. VS MISHRILAL - (2003)9 SCC 426, and the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the case and counter case should be tried together by the same court irrespective of the nature of offence involved.

entities.text: STATE OF M.P. VS MISHRILAL - (2003)9 SCC 426
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The rational behind this is to avoid conflicting judgment over the same incident because if cross cases are allowed to be tried by two courts separately, there is likelihood of conflicting judgments.

9. This Court in the case of ABDUL MAJID SAB VS STATE OF KARNATAKA - ILR 2010 KAR 1719,
has held that the same Investigating Officer should investigate both the case viz., case and counter case and shall file the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3599 final report and the case and counter case should be conducted by separate prosecutors.

entities.text: ABDUL MAJID SAB VS STATE OF KARNATAKA - ILR 2010 KAR 1719
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. So far as the power under Section 482 Cr.PC to quash the proceedings, in a case and counter case is concerned, having regard to the fact that the incident in question is not in dispute so also the spot of crime, in normal circumstances, the High Court should not venture to quash the proceedings when it is found that there is a case and counter case in respect of the same incident between the same parties.

However, if the averments made in the complaint prima facie show that necessary ingredients for the alleged offences is absent and proceedings is initiated only as a counter blast to the complaint lodged by the other party, in the said event, the inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C, can be exercised by this Court.
11. In the case on hand, perusal of the averments made in the complaint would go to show that there are sufficient materials to prosecute the accused for the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3599 alleged offences.
Under the circumstances, there cannot be any interference as against the impugned proceedings.
I do not find any good ground to entertain this petition.

12. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
Sd/-
